If cancer is supposed to just be a regular cell that goes through mitosis differently, could a person made entirely out of cancerous tissue live regularly?
Would it be possible to create a functioning human entirely out of cancerous tissue?

That's an interesting question. I would probably lean towards no, since my (extremely limited) understanding is that the main problem with cancer cells is that the thing that tells them to stop growing is missing/broken and that they also don't stay where they belong as well (like breast tissue growing in your lungs). So if you could have a person made entirely out of cancer cells that somehow all stay where that particular cell belongs and the cells all grow/divide at proportional rates, the person probably would probably end up growing nonstop until the weight of the top half crushed the bottom half.

Probably not a normal life.

The main cause of death in the vast majority of cancer patients is metastatic spread. This is when cells from a tumor move and invade other tissue systems. If tumors only kept growing in an uncontrolled fashion Avastin and surgery would have been the cure.

Unfortunately, things that prevent tumor size growth, such as Avastin, can cause metastasis. A Co worker of mine is doing awesome, but sad research on how trying to stop tumor growth by preventing blood vessel growth often increases metastasis.

So I agree with your conclusion that using genetically abnormal cells in some crazy human generator would probably fail but for a great deal more reasons than size.

First, a cancer cell can be much more than just a non cycle regulated cell. There are so many things that can go wrong. If the P53 gene gets hit, future DNA damage won't get noticed. This is a common cause of cancer. If this was not rectified prior to some "human generation" technique that your referring to the new creature would not be able to respond to things from UV damage to free radicals and would die.

One of the major milestones of Cancer research came when some bad ass English surgeon realized that Metastasis occurred in a seed-and soil fashion. This means that certain cancerous cell regions are more prone to migration to other regions. This metastasis is what kills most patients. There are a variety of genetic issues that allow metastasis to occur, from increased angiogenesis to deleterious errors in the regulation of adhesion proteins. If this was not fixed than this new creature would have cells getting up and colonizing new regions of the body constantly. This would be terrible. Think about how small and essential your kidneys are. A small growth of migrants can destroy the functioning of a nephron bundle very quickly,, leading to negative clinical outcomes.
